title: Linked List Components
statement:
`head` is the first node of a singly linked list whose values are all different, and `nums` is an array of distinct values, each of which appears somewhere in the list. Walk along the list and group together nodes that sit next to each other and whose values are all in `nums`; each such group is extended as far as possible in both directions, so a node whose value is not in `nums` (or the end of the list) separates groups. Return how many groups there are.

The order of the values inside `nums` does not matter; only the order of the nodes in the list does.
constraints: The list has n nodes, with 1 <= n <= 10^4
All values in nums are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

A group ends exactly once: at its last node, where the next node is either missing or not in `nums`. So counting groups is the same as counting nodes that are in `nums` while their successor is not. Putting `nums` into a hash set makes each membership test O(1), so a single walk along the list is enough. (The slow version searches the array `nums` for every node, which is O(n · m).)

## Approach

1. Put every value of `nums` into the set `wanted`.
2. Walk the list with `node`, starting at `head`.
3. For each node, compute `inside` (its value is in `wanted`) and `nextInside` (a next node exists and its value is in `wanted`).
4. If `inside` is true and `nextInside` is false, a group ends here, so increase `count`.
5. Move to `node.next`; when the list ends, return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

List `0 → 1 → 2 → 3`, `wanted = {0, 1, 3}`.

- Node 0: inside, next (1) is inside. No group ends.
- Node 1: inside, next (2) is not. A group ends: `count = 1`.
- Node 2: not inside.
- Node 3: inside, no next node. A group ends: `count = 2`.

The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m): building the set and one walk over the n nodes.
- Space: O(m) for the set of the m values in `nums`.

## Pitfalls

- Check `node.next !== null` before reading `node.next.val`; the last node may end a group.
- The order of `nums` is irrelevant; adjacency is decided by the list, not by the array.
- Counting nodes in `nums` instead of groups overcounts any run longer than one node.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `wanted` | set of the values in `nums` |
| `count` | number of groups that have ended so far |
| `node` | the current list node |
| `inside` | whether the current node's value is in `wanted` |
| `nextInside` | whether a next node exists and its value is in `wanted` |

narration.4: Start the walk at the first node.
narration.6: Visit every node of the list once.

narration.8: Is there a next node, and is its value chosen too?
narration.9: A chosen node followed by a gap or the end is the last node of a group.
narration.14: Every group has been counted at its last node.
